method.archived_trace: Three 48-frame Radeon 8060S passes from 2026-10-31, one decode worker and two-frame lead. A slow displayed interval is greater than 41.67 ms; the frame split uses consecutive shown timestamps.
method.decode_probe: Warm-page-cache 1080p native-half EXR. The playback read_media_raster decoder ran in synchronized batches for 10 rounds at each worker count. OpenImageIO-only decode and a concurrent 256 MiB NumPy copy were diagnostic controls.

largest_slow_minus_fast_difference.interpretation: Slow frames spend more time in preview-thread Python orchestration and Transform staging. Decoded-source waiting is 1.130 ms lower on slow frames, so it does not bind this p95 tail.

decode_contention_probe_ms.verdict: The full playback decoder does not serialize in isolation: two and three concurrent decodes remain within 2 percent of its one-thread median. The playback slowdown therefore needs the live preview's Roto/source/scheduling contention; raw EXR decode alone is neither a GIL nor a memory-bandwidth explanation. OpenImageIO-only work slows under concurrency, but that smaller component does not reproduce full decoder behavior.

proposed_fixes.proposal: Trace and remove preview-thread head-of-line work around Transform preparation; cache immutable Transform setup or move it into the island encoder.
proposed_fixes.reason: This is the largest slow-minus-fast difference, with Transform preparation adding 1.455 ms inside it.

proposed_fixes.proposal: Measure and decouple live Roto/source scheduling from decode-ahead readiness before changing decode-worker counts.
proposed_fixes.reason: Slow frames wait less than fast frames, and isolated full decodes scale across threads; a worker-count change has no measured tail saving.

proposed_fixes.proposal: Profile the Transform kernel separately and reduce its dispatch/encode preparation only after the preview-thread trace identifies the shared delay.
proposed_fixes.reason: GPU kernel time rises only 0.142 ms on slow frames, so kernel tuning cannot close this tail by itself.

gate_verdict: No. The independent measured tail differences total about 2.9 ms, below the 5.275 ms needed to bring the archived 53.634 ms p95 to 41.67 ms; the proposed items also overlap. A larger live scheduling or full-frame pipeline change needs evidence before claiming the gate is reachable.
